questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere, where the main language was English but I also wanted to go somewhere that was very different from what I am used to. Canada was the perfect place for me as it seemed familiar but also quite different from Europe and Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really liked being abroad and getting to explore a new setting.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Because of the Covid-19 pandemic I needed to get a study permit, which is not usually needed when going for just one semester. To get the study permit I needed to get my biometric taken and this is only possible to do in either Berlin or Stockholm, which ment that I had to do a trip during my exams in June in order to get my application processed. I found that it was generally hard to find the information needed as the guidelines kept changing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: University of Toronto did not really provide any assistance apart from a few mails. We had an online orientation which was pretty much the only information we got. But I think the lack of assistance was due to the covid-19 pandemic as the university was not able to do events as a welcome to the students from abroad.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were a few options for on campus housing which was marketed on the University of Toronto website. I found my housing through google and was able to live on campus at a reasonable price.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had a common kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Campus Coop which is an organisation with multiple houses around the St. George campus. The houses were generally in good shape but the house I lived in had a very small kitchen which made it quite hard to cook as we were 14 people sharing one oven and stove.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of housing is quite expensive and not that much better than the cheaper options so I recommend doing a bit of research before committing to anything.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was hard as a sociology student to figure out if i was even able to live up to the prerequisites set by the University.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to fill out a google analysis for each course that we wanted to take.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were some websites to guide us but it was really hard to figure out what was possible.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I registered for so in the end it worked out.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend being mindfull of what is required to be a full-time student and not register for too many courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I chose 200 level courses mainly

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The way of teaching was quite different than at UCPH and there were a lot of work during the semester instead of in the end, which is what I was used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Urban Sociology 
Sociology of Crime and Deviance
Introduction to Environmental Studies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked Urban Sociology

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to get a mandatory ensurance provided by the university which was quite expensive and I was not told that I was supposed to print out something or register again in order for it to work so I am not even sure I would have been able to use it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I was quite surprised that the groceries where generally quite expensive. Especially dairy and bread.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of sports opportunities as well as cultural but these where mainly shut down due to covid-19.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not do a lot of university provided activities as they were not available at my stay but I recommend using the sports facilities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going to the Toronto Islands especially in the summer where you can swim in the lake.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly met Europeans

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I was surprised how much smalltalk is expected of you in Canada.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really liked how the city had a lot of different neighborhoods and how they were very different from each other.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Give yourself the opportunity to explore the city and walk around and not be buried in schoolwork all the time. 

2. Visit the Toronto Islands

3. Go see either a hockey or basketball game in Scotia Bank Arena

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Walk or bike around the city instead of using the public transportation (which is generally really bad and always late). When you walk around you really get to know the city and being away from home you have the time to walk everywhere.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I found it very rewarding to be able to just walk around and not have the usual responsibilities that I have at home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was being away from my friends and family as well as my room at home. It took some time for me to adjust to living somewhere else.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I would recommend doing something to make your living space nice. I bought some small decorative things to make it feel more like home and I really think it helped with getting myself comfortable so I was able to explore and enjoy the experience. The room you have is very much your relaxation base and this is an important place to feel good.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
